title: Canada Fights Back: New Tariffs on U.S. Goods
summary:
Imagine your best friend suddenly started charging you money to borrow their toys. That's kind of what's happening between the U.S. and Canada right now—but with real stuff like cars and food.

On Tuesday, Canada put new taxes (called tariffs) on about $20 billion worth of American goods. Some taxes are as high as 50%! That means if a U.S. company wants to sell something in Canada, they have to pay a big extra fee. Canada did this because the U.S. put tariffs on Canadian stuff first. It's like a snowball fight that keeps getting bigger.

But it's not just about money. Many Canadians feel hurt. President Trump keeps saying Canada should become the 51st state! That makes Canadians angry. Some are even boycotting American products and not traveling to the U.S. anymore.

Chrystia Freeland knows a lot about this. She used to be Canada's finance minister and helped make a big trade deal with the U.S. and Mexico. She says the U.S. is making a mistake by being mean to its friends. She said, "It has to start with stopping punching your friends in the face, which is what Washington is doing right now." Ouch!

Freeland also said that even though the U.S. is 10 times bigger than Canada, that doesn't mean they should always get their way. She remembers someone once told her that because the U.S. is bigger, they should get their way 10 times more. She said that's not how partnerships work.

So, what happens next? Nobody knows. But one thing is for sure: when friends fight, everyone feels it. Maybe they'll work it out soon!
why_it_matters: When countries that trade with each other start fighting over taxes, prices of food, cars, and other goods can go up, so this fight could show up in your own family's shopping cart.

background_read: The U.S. and Canada (America's neighbor to the north) are usually among each other's biggest trading partners, so tariffs can hurt both sides.
Tariffs (taxes on imported goods) make products more expensive and are often answered with more tariffs.
President Trump (the U.S. president) has angered Canada by putting tariffs on Canadian goods and by saying Canada should become the 51st state.
Article_Structure: WHO: Canada and the United States, with Canadian leaders and former finance minister Chrystia Freeland speaking out.
WHAT: Canada placed new tariffs, some as high as 50%, on about $20 billion of American goods in response to U.S. tariffs.
WHERE: Across the U.S.-Canada border and in the trade between the two countries.
WHY: Canada feels hurt because the U.S. put tariffs first and President Trump has suggested Canada should become the 51st state.

perspectives.description: They see the U.S. taxes as unfair treatment of a friend, and some are boycotting American products.
They argue tariffs can protect American workers and push other countries to make fairer trade deals.

perspectives.perspective: Businesses and families on both sides
perspectives.description: They worry about higher prices and about hurt feelings between two countries that usually work well together.
